teach.goal: Como não traduzir palavra por palavra.

group: Compare erro e forma natural: Could you to open the window? → Could you open the window? | You could open the window? → Could you open the window, please? | Could you opened the window? → Could you open the window?.

facts.big: Could you / Could I + verbo base
facts.label: Pedidos educados com could
facts.sub: Use Could you + verbo base para pedir algo e Could I + verbo base para pedir permissão: Could you open the window, please? Could I leave my suitcase?

facts.label: Pedido educado
facts.sub: Use Could you + verbo base para pedir algo com educação: Could you open the window, please? Não use to depois de could. Adicione please para soar mais gentil.

facts.label: Permissão
facts.sub: Use Could I + verbo base para pedir permissão: Could I leave my suitcase here? Soa mais educado que Can I…? Muito usado em hotéis, lojas e restaurantes.

facts.label: Respostas
facts.sub: Para responder, use Of course, Certainly ou Sure. Para recusar com educação, diga Sorry, I’m afraid not. Evite No sozinho, porque soa seco.

facts.label: Por favor e obrigado
facts.sub: Acrescente please no fim do pedido e thank you depois da resposta. Could you wake me up at six thirty, please? Isso mostra respeito e ajuda você a ser bem atendido.

pages.title: A small hotel · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a cool evening in Denver, and the mountains are dark. Sara arrives at a small hotel after a long trip. Her room is on the third floor, near the stairs. The room is warm and the air is heavy. Moe, the night receptionist, knocks on the door. He asks if she needs anything.

“Good evening, Ms. Sara. Is everything all right with your room?” says Moe. “Almost. It’s very hot. Could you open the window, please?” says Sara. “Of course. Could I also turn on the fan for you?” says Moe.
